items.title: Jobs & gap check
items.goal: Recruiters create and edit client jobs in a form, or upload the client's job description and confirm what was read into the same form. Every save stores a version, and the portal lists what is missing, unclear, contradictory or unfair in the request, each with a question to ask the client. Open flags never block matching.
prd: Job matching → Job input (decided): recruiters create a job with a form or upload the job description, which is read into the same form to confirm → decided
Job matching → requirement 1: nationality and language count only when marked as a real requirement with a written reason → decided
Job matching → requirement 3: the form marks each requirement must-have or nice-to-have → proposed
Job request gap check → Scope (decided): client job requests only; CVs are not checked → decided
Job request gap check → flag types: missing (approved); uncertain, conflicting, fair employment (proposed)
Job request gap check → requirements 1 and 2 (why it matters, client question, resolve or dismiss with a note) → proposed; requirement 3 (open flags don't block matching) → decided
Main flows → Saving a job: store a new version, run the gap check, re-score after the response is sent → suggested
exit: A recruiter can create, edit and version a job, and nationality or language cannot count without a written reason
An uploaded job description pre-fills the form and the recruiter confirms it before saving
Every missing-field rule in the PRD raises a flag with a question for the client
The job shows a banner counting open flags, and matching still runs
outOfScope: Checking CVs for gaps — the PRD limits the gap check to job requests
Sending anything to a client: the portal never emails and never shares with clients
Client logins or approval workflows — non-goals
Rewriting the job description for the client

items.title: Recruiters create and edit client jobs
items.story: As a recruiter, I want to capture a client's job request with its must-haves marked, so that matching knows what actually matters and I can defend how a score was reached.
ac: Given the job form, when I mark a requirement, then I must choose must-have or nice-to-have.
Given I mark nationality or language as required, when I try to save without writing why, then the save is refused and the reason field is shown as required.
Given I save a job, when the save succeeds, then a new job version is stored and the previous version is still readable.
Given the jobs list, when I open it, then each job shows its status, owner, open gap-flag count and candidates per stage.
prd: Job matching → Job input (decided) → decided
Job matching → requirement 1: nationality and language only with a written reason → decided
Job matching → requirement 3: must-have and nice-to-have → proposed
Data model → jobs, job_versions → suggested
UI design → Jobs and Job form screens → decided

items.title: Build the job form and its Server Action with the requirement-reason rule
items.what: Build the job form from `design/specs/job-form.md` and the Server Action behind it: owner name, client, requirements each marked must-have or nice-to-have, and the rule that nationality or language may only be required alongside a written reason. Test-first: the validation rule is logic with a compliance consequence.
scope: A Zod schema shared by the form and the Server Action
Failing tests first: nationality required without a reason is rejected; language required without a reason is rejected; a reason of only whitespace is rejected; both are accepted with a reason
Requirement rows with a must-have / nice-to-have choice
The form built from the design spec, with validation and error states
exclusions: The jobs list and detail screens (T03)
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover all four reason cases
A job cannot be saved with nationality or language required and no written reason, in the form and in the action
Every requirement carries a must-have or nice-to-have marking
Playwright covers the refused save and the accepted save at both widths

items.title: Store a new job version on every save
items.what: Every save writes a new immutable job version, and the job points at its current one. Match scores are keyed to a job version, so this is what stops an old score being shown against changed requirements. Test-first.
scope: Versioning in the save path: insert a version, move the job's current-version pointer, never mutate an old version
Failing tests first: two saves produce two versions; the pointer follows the latest; an old version's fields are unchanged; saving without a change still versions or is explicitly documented not to
A read helper that always resolves the current version
The version id is what scoring and gap flags attach to
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover version creation, pointer movement and immutability of old versions
Gap flags and match scores attach to a job version, not to the job
The no-change save behaviour is decided in the spec and covered by a test

items.title: Build the jobs list and job detail screens
items.what: Build the two screens from `design/specs/jobs.md` and `design/specs/job-detail.md`: the list with status, owner, open flag count and candidates per stage; the detail with requirements and the sections the later phases fill in.
scope: Jobs list as a Server Component with the four columns the PRD names
Job detail showing requirements and the version it is showing, with placeholders for the ranked matches and pipeline board that later phases fill
Tables collapsing to cards at phone width
Playwright coverage at both widths with the shared assertions
done: The list shows status, owner, open gap-flag count and candidates per stage for each job
Job detail names the job version it is displaying
Both screens match their design specs on review at desktop and phone width
Playwright passes at both widths including the overflow assertion

items.title: An uploaded job description pre-fills the job form
items.story: As a recruiter, I want to upload the client's job description and have the form filled in for me to check, so that I am correcting a draft rather than retyping a document.
ac: Given a PDF or Word job description, when I upload it, then its fields are read into the same job form for me to confirm.
Given the pre-filled form, when I look at a field the AI filled, then it is labelled as a suggestion and shows the text it came from.
Given I confirm the form, when it saves, then the job is created exactly as I confirmed it, not as the AI proposed it.
prd: Job matching → Job input (decided): an uploaded description is read into the same form for the recruiter to confirm → decided
AI governance → requirement 1: every AI output shows the text it was based on → proposed
AI pipeline → every AI step returns JSON checked against a fixed schema → suggested

items.title: Write the job-description extraction prompt and schema
items.what: Write the schema and prompt that turn a client's job description into the job form's fields, in English and Simplified Chinese, with verbatim evidence for each field and the shared prompt rules.
scope: `src/ai/prompts/extract-jd/`: schema matching the job form's fields, prompt v1, fictional examples in both languages
Every extracted field carries the job-description text it came from
The model proposes must-have and nice-to-have but never decides them; the recruiter confirms
Prompt-injection handling: instructions inside the job description are ignored and reported
A prompt version recorded on every run
done: The schema covers every field of the job form and requires evidence text
Fictional English and Simplified Chinese examples are included
The prompt states that must-have and nice-to-have are proposals for the recruiter to confirm
The prompt carries a version the service records

items.title: Build upload, extract and pre-fill for the job form
items.what: Let a recruiter upload a job description, store the original in the private bucket, extract its fields with one model call, and present the job form pre-filled with every AI-filled value labelled as a suggestion and showing its source text.
scope: Upload through a route handler with type and size validation, storing the original privately
One extraction call through the shared wrapper, logged to `ai_runs`
The job form rendered pre-filled, with `AiSuggestion` and `SourceQuote` on every AI-filled field
Failing tests first: a schema-invalid extraction does not pre-fill anything; an unsupported file is rejected with a reason; the saved job holds the recruiter's confirmed values, not the AI's
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover invalid extraction, unsupported file, and recruiter-confirmed values winning
Every pre-filled field is labelled as a suggestion and shows its source text
The original job description is stored in the private bucket and reachable only through a signed link
Playwright covers upload, confirm and save at both widths

items.title: Missing information is flagged with a question for the client
items.story: As a recruiter, I want the portal to tell me what the client left out and exactly what to ask them, so that I go back to the client once with a complete list instead of three times.
ac: Given a saved job with no salary range, when the gap check runs, then a missing-salary flag appears with a question to ask the client.
Given each of the PRD's missing-field rules, when the field is absent, then exactly one flag is raised for it.
Given a field is present, when the gap check runs, then no missing flag is raised for it.
prd: Job request gap check → Missing fields (approved): salary range, location or work arrangement, employment type, headcount, start date, must-have skills, interview steps → decided
Job request gap check → requirement 1: each flag shows why it matters and a suggested question for the client → proposed
AI pipeline → Gap check: code checks for missing fields → suggested

items.title: Implement the missing-field rules in code with a question for each
items.what: The PRD's missing-field checks are deterministic, so they belong in code rather than in a model call. Implement one rule per approved missing field, each producing a flag with why it matters and a question to ask the client. Test-first.
scope: One rule per approved field: salary range, location or work arrangement, employment type, headcount, start date, must-have skills, interview steps
Failing tests first: each rule fires when its field is absent and stays silent when present; an empty string or whitespace counts as absent; exactly one flag per rule
Each flag carries a stable type, why it matters, and a suggested client question in recruiter language
Flags written against the job version
exclusions: The model-based uncertain, conflicting and fair-employment flags (E05-S04)
Blocking matching — open flags never block it
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover every approved missing-field rule, present and absent
Each flag stores its type, why it matters and a client question
Whitespace-only values count as missing, proven by a test
Flags attach to the job version that was saved

items.title: Uncertain, conflicting and unfair requirements are flagged
items.story: As a recruiter, I want vague wording, contradictions between the job description and the form, and requirements that breach fair-employment guidelines pointed out before I start sourcing, so that I am not the last person to notice.
ac: Given a job saying "competitive salary", when the gap check runs, then an uncertain flag appears quoting that text with a question for the client.
Given an uploaded job description that contradicts the form on salary or location, when the gap check runs, then a conflicting flag appears quoting both sources.
Given a requirement that prefers an age, gender, race or religion, when the gap check runs, then a fair-employment flag appears explaining why it is a problem in Singapore.
Given any flag, when I read it, then it quotes the text it came from and is labelled as a suggestion.
prd: Job request gap check → Uncertain, Conflicting, Fair employment flag types → proposed
Job request gap check → requirement 1: why it matters and a suggested client question → proposed
AI pipeline → Gap check: one model call finds uncertain, conflicting and fair-employment issues → suggested
Fair employment → TAFEP guidelines; Workplace Fairness Act from end-2027 → noted

items.title: Write the gap-check prompt and schema for uncertain, conflicting and fair-employment flags
items.what: Write the schema and prompt for the one model call that finds vague wording, contradictions between the job description and the form, and requirements that breach Singapore's fair-employment guidelines — each with verbatim evidence, why it matters, and a question to ask the client.
scope: `src/ai/prompts/gap-check/`: schema with the three flag types, prompt v1, fictional examples in English and Simplified Chinese
Every flag requires a verbatim quote; a conflicting flag requires a quote from each source
Fair-employment guidance grounded in the TAFEP attributes the PRD names, with the Workplace Fairness Act attributes noted as a future extension, not silently added
The prompt never proposes rejecting a candidate or contacting a client
A prompt version recorded on every run
exclusions: The missing-field rules, which are code (E05-S03-T01)
Adding scoring on any protected attribute
done: The schema covers the three proposed flag types and requires evidence for each
Conflicting flags require a quote from both the form and the job description
Fictional English and Simplified Chinese examples are included
The prompt records that the Workplace Fairness Act attributes are out of scope until the compliance review decides otherwise

items.title: Build the gap-check service with one call per save and evidence verification
items.what: Run one gap-check call when a job is saved, validate its output, verify every quote appears verbatim in the source, store the flags against the job version, and log the run. Test-first with a fake model.
scope: `src/server/gap-check/run.ts` called from the job save path, combining the code rules and the model flags

Failing tests first: a flag whose quote is not in the source is dropped and reported; a schema-invalid response raises no flags rather than partial ones; the same job saved twice does not duplicate flags
Every run written to `ai_runs` with model, version, prompt version, cost and duration
Flags stored against the job version with their evidence
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover invented quotes, schema failure and duplicate flags
Every gap-check run writes one `ai_runs` row with its cost and duration
Flags carry their evidence and attach to the job version
The job save still succeeds when the gap check fails, with the failure recorded

items.title: Recruiters resolve or dismiss flags without blocking matching
items.story: As a recruiter, I want to tick off a flag once I have asked the client, with a note about what they said, so that my colleagues can see where the request stands without asking me.
ac: Given a flag, when I mark it resolved or dismissed, then I must add a short note and my typed name is recorded.
Given open flags on a job, when I open it, then a banner shows how many are open.
Given a job with open flags, when matching runs, then it runs normally and the flags do not block it.
prd: Job request gap check → requirement 2: the recruiter marks each flag resolved or dismissed, with a short note → proposed
Job request gap check → requirement 3: open flags don't block matching; the job shows a banner with the number still open → decided
Users → every change is logged with the name the recruiter types → decided

items.title: Add resolve and dismiss with a required note and typed name
items.what: Let a recruiter close a flag as resolved or dismissed, requiring a short note and recording their typed name. Test-first: the note and name requirements are the audit trail.
scope: A Server Action with Zod validation for resolve and dismiss

Failing tests first: an empty or whitespace note is refused; a missing typed name is refused; resolving stores the state, note, name and time; a resolved flag cannot be silently re-opened without a new record
The flag's history preserved rather than overwritten
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover the empty note, the missing name, and a successful resolve and dismiss
Every state change records the typed name and the time
A flag's earlier state remains readable after it is closed

items.title: Build the gap-flag checklist and the open-flag banner on job detail
items.what: Build the flag checklist on job detail from `design/specs/job-detail.md`: each flag with why it matters, its quoted evidence, the question to ask the client, and resolve or dismiss; plus the banner counting what is still open.
scope: The checklist grouped by flag type, using `AiSuggestion` and `SourceQuote` on every model-derived flag
Resolve and dismiss with the note field and the typed-name prompt
The banner showing the open count and stating that matching is not blocked
Playwright coverage at both widths
exclusions: Sending the question to the client — the portal never contacts clients
done: Every model-derived flag is labelled as a suggestion and shows its quoted evidence
Resolving requires a note and prompts for the typed name on first use
The banner shows the open count and says matching still runs
Playwright passes at desktop and phone width
